```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true

markets <- read_parquet("data/markets.parquet")
groups <- read_parquet("data/groups.parquet")
market_groups <- read_parquet("data/market_groups.parquet")
history <- read_parquet("data/history.parquet")

joined <- history |>
  left_join(markets |> select(market_id, outcome, resolved_at), by = "market_id") |>
  mutate(
    outcome_numeric = case_when(
      outcome == "YES" ~ 1,
      outcome == "NO" ~ 0,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    absolute_error = abs(probability - outcome_numeric),
    days_to_resolution = as.integer(as.Date(resolved_at) - date),
    time_bucket = case_when(
      days_to_resolution > 90 ~ "More than 90 days",
      days_to_resolution > 30 ~ "30 to 90 days",
      days_to_resolution > 7 ~ "7 to 30 days",
      days_to_resolution > 0 ~ "1 to 7 days",
      days_to_resolution == 0 ~ "Final day"
    ),
    time_bucket = factor(
      time_bucket,
      levels = c(
        "More than 90 days",
        "30 to 90 days",
        "7 to 30 days",
        "1 to 7 days",
        "Final day"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
```

`market_groups` is the bridge table: its `market_id` links to `markets`, and its
`group_slug` links to `groups`. A market can therefore belong to multiple groups.

```{r}
topic_join <- markets |>
  left_join(market_groups, by = "market_id")

tibble(
  original_market_rows = nrow(markets),
  topic_join_rows = nrow(topic_join)
) |>
  print()

accuracy <- joined |>
  group_by(time_bucket) |>
  summarise(
    mean_absolute_error = mean(absolute_error),
    n_snapshots = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(accuracy)

ggplot(accuracy, aes(x = time_bucket, y = mean_absolute_error, group = 1)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Prediction markets get smarter near the deadline",
    subtitle = "Mean absolute error in Manifold Markets forecasts, by days remaining",
    x = "Days remaining",
    y = "Mean absolute error"
  )
```

```{r}
joined |>
  filter(days_to_resolution == 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = probability)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Final-day forecast probabilities",
    x = "Predicted probability of YES",
    y = "Snapshot count"
  )
```

```{r}
calibration <- joined |>
  filter(days_to_resolution == 0) |>
  mutate(
    probability_bin = cut(
      probability,
      breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
      labels = paste0(
        seq(0, 90, by = 10), "% to ",
        seq(10, 100, by = 10), "%"
      ),
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(probability_bin) |>
  summarise(
    predicted_probability = mean(probability),
    actual_rate = mean(outcome_numeric),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(calibration)

ggplot(
  calibration,
  aes(x = predicted_probability, y = actual_rate, size = n)
) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Markets in bin") +
  labs(
    title = "Do final-day predictions match observed YES rates?",
    x = "Mean predicted probability",
    y = "Actual YES rate"
  )
```
